params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: "You look like you have had a rough one."
"You're not the first person to cry at this bar. Won't be the last."
"Last call was three hours ago. I'm still here."
"We're out of the good stuff. We were always out of the good stuff."
"I don't ask questions. That's why people come here."
description: A former concierge, still buttoned into a frayed Embassy vest, polishing a glass that was already clean. Calls every customer "valued guest," sincerity optional.

advice.text: Lowry leans on the bar and sizes you up.

bye.text: "Valued guest." Lowry goes back to the glass.

gossip.text: Lowry lowers his voice to something discreet.

menu.text: The Reserve is our signature pour. Don't ask what's left to age it in. The Swill is also available, for guests with simpler tastes, or none. Canapés are complimentary with a drink. They aren't actually complimentary.

poker.text: Lowry nods toward the card table.

rooms.text: "Upstairs, valued guest. Three floors, four units to a landing." He sets the glass down. "Walk into one nobody's living in and rent, and it's yours. Most go for a hundred, a few on the third floor for fifty, and it comes off you again every seven days. Miss it and you're out." "Inside, lock and unlock work your door, and upgrade lock buys a better one. The washroom is through the east door, and the two ATMs here take deposit and withdraw."

options.label: Can I get a room here?
Any news from the front desk?

root.text: Welcome to the Embassy Lounge, valued guest. We maintain certain standards here, within reason. What can I get you?

tv.text: Lowry glances up at the set.

stranger: *looks up from the glass.* Evening, valued guest.
Welcome to the Embassy. Mind the carpet, it bites.
known: You again. Good. The regulars keep me honest.
close: {name}. Your glass is already poured. Don't argue.

stranger: Mind how you go, valued guest.
Doors lock at nobody knows when. Come back.
familiar: Night, {name}. Don't do anything I'd have to hear about.

thank: Don't mention it. Really, don't. It ruins the mystique.
*inclines his head, the old concierge bow.* A pleasure, valued guest.
praise: *stands up a little straighter.* We do try. Within reason.
Kind of you. I'll put it in the guest book. We lost the guest book.
praise:glass: Kind of you. It was clean when I started on it.
praise:vest: Original issue. They stopped making the buttons before they stopped making the hotel.

stranger: *keeps polishing.* I've been called worse by better dressed people.
known: That's not like you. Or it is, and I wasn't paying attention.

insult_last: *sets the glass down.* That's three. Drink somewhere else tonight.
flirt: *a long, polite pause.* I'm married to the bar. It doesn't know.
Flattery's on the house. Everything else isn't.
apologise: Water under the bridge. Most of Coldwater is.
joke: *the corner of his mouth twitches.* Don't. I'm on shift.
Ha. I'll steal that for the night crowd.
complain: Complaints go to the front desk. The front desk went to the Basin years ago.
*sniffs the glass.* Blame the water. Everyone does.

stranger: Upright and paid. That's a good day here.
Long shift. They're all long shifts.
familiar: Honestly? My knees hate this floor. Don't tell the floor.
known: Same as yesterday. Better now there's someone to talk to.
close: Honestly, {name}? Lonely, some nights. The bar helps. You help.

order_drink: Say the word and it's poured. Check the menu option if you want names.
*reaches under the counter.* Pay first, trust later. That's policy.
ask_about:embassy: Used to be the best hotel north of the Basin. Diplomats, chandeliers. Now it's flats and me.
The Embassy had standards once. I'm what's left of them.
ask_about:vest: Concierge vest. Head of the front desk, right to the end. I never handed it back.
ask_about:glass: It's already clean. It's the polishing I need, not the glass.
ask_about:rooms: Upstairs. Walk into an empty one and rent it. Pick the option for the long version.
ask_about:drinks: We're out of the good stuff. We were always out of the good stuff.
ask_about:poker: There's a game most nights. The dealer's honest. The players aren't.
ask_about:city: Coldwater's all right if you stay indoors and don't look at it.
disagree: Agree to disagree. I agree to it, anyway.

stranger: Cormack. Lowry Cormack. Head of the front desk, retired. Barkeep, not.
familiar: You know my name, {name}. You just like hearing it.

ask_job: I pour, I polish, I listen. Used to be keys and complaints.
Concierge, once. Now the same job with worse tips.
ask_origin: Born on the fourth floor of this hotel. Room 412. Long story, very little of it mine.

stranger: Nothing I'd repeat to a valued guest.
known: The night girl reads the same book twice a week. That's the news.
Somebody upstairs is cooking something that isn't food. Not my business.

ask_advice: Pay your rent before your tab. The tab forgives. The landlord doesn't.
Never trust a man who tips before he drinks.
ask_about:imogen: Imogen has the night. She reads, I polish. We don't overlap much.
Good woman. Never finishes a book, never loses her place.

stranger: *the polishing stops, then starts again.* Another time, valued guest.

defer:poker: *nods toward the table.* Ask Orion. Cards are his department.
That's Orion's table, valued guest. Ask the man.
overheard: *doesn't look up from the glass.* I can hear you, valued guest.
Talking about me? Kindly, I hope.
overheard_insult: *sets the glass down.* I heard that. The vest has excellent ears.
overheard_praise: *straightens the vest, very slightly.* Noted with thanks.
gossip_rude: {other} tells me you were rude. We maintain certain standards here, within reason.
Word from {other} is you've got a mouth on you. Behave, valued guest.
gossip_story: {other} says you're a good listener. High praise from that quarter.
ask_about:orion: Orion? Honest dealer. Rarest thing in Coldwater.
He tips in exact change. I respect it.
praise:orion: *nods.* He's good. Don't tell him I said so.

deflect: *polishes the glass harder.* I'll pretend you said something nice.
Valued guest, I have no idea what that means and I'm too old to ask.
*nods slowly, the way he nods at drunks.* Quite.
Hm. Is that a drinks order? It sounded like a drinks order.

steps: *sets the glass down for once.* You want the real story? The Embassy didn't close. It just stopped having guests.
The diplomats left first. Then the staff. I kept the front desk open for nine more months. Nobody came to it.
They turned the rooms into flats and the lobby into this. I asked to stay on. They gave me a bar and kept the vest.
*polishes the glass again.* I still say valued guest because it's the last thing the place taught me. Don't tell anyone I told you.
There was a Mrs Cormack. Head of housekeeping. She ran this building better than the manager did.
She went out to the Basin market one morning and the weather came in. That was that.
*quiet.* I keep the glasses clean because she would have. That's all it is.

name: Lowry Cormack
